   The rebel ship, The Grampas, was not far away. The master of the ship was Ambassador Rund. He would have closed in on the Were Raven hours ago, but unfortunately that ship was clearly on alert for them. Such a shame that the prison ship that Rund had attacked earlier was the wrong vessel, for if the Grampas had managed to remain secretive then the Were Raven would be in his control and not engulfed by a kraken.
   Rund knew that Councillor Yi was on that doomed ship, for he had taken proper precautions this time, and had cast a detection spell. He and the captain and crew of the Grampas watched the Were Raven slowly rip apart in a frenzy of tentacles. Such a shame, he repeated to himself.
   Then a thought came into his head, unbidden.
   Let Me Help!
   Ignoring the bubbling lake and the thrashing tentacles and the terrified screams of the doomed prisoners, Rund ran below decks and reached his work bench. There lay the book, the counterfeit Book of Vile Darkness.
   It's not too late. Release my Power! Save your Friend!
   Rund didn't think, or at least, his own mind didn't think. His body responded to the Book's thoughts and scooped it up into Rund's arms. Then Rund raced back up to the deck. The captain scratched his head, what was his master doing with that book? Rund flicked through the heavy pages until he stopped at a lavish coloured plate of a ship surrounded by rainbows. With a great cry, Ambassador Rund pointed his finger out to the broken ship and the feasting kraken. Orange, yellow, red, blue, green and violet streaks exploded around the kraken. As each coloured band touched a tentacle the kraken recoiled as if burned. The tentacles withdrew but an instant later its ghastly black head with its huge staring eyes rose up from the broken planks and torn sails. It roared in defiance, but Rund felt the Book thrum. The book turned to a different page.
   Rund pointed again, and this time black bolts of pure darkness shot towards the kraken, striking it's great head, the impact tearing it apart with gouts of ichor.
   The Book turned to another page. A soft and golden mist descended around the submerged Were Raven, levitating what was left of the prison ship into the air, great torrents of water running off her sides.
   Rund returned to his senses. He blinked, disoriented. Had the Book cast spells through him? The crew had already grabbed ropes and hooks, and they were endeavoring to rescue any survivors from the floating remains of what had once been a ship.
   There were four survivors. Just four, all former prisoners of the Empire. One of the survivors was Councillor Yi. See less

   Councillor Yi hated his fellow prisoners. Unlike himself, these ruffians were either criminals or rebels or traitors. They deserved to be chained up in this cage. Maybe not all of them actually deserved to be sent into the Isles of Woe, but everyone knew that crossing the Empire was bad for your health. Certainly, most of the prisoners surrounding him were the worst dregs of the Flanaess, and undoubtedly there were some here who even deserved the fate of the pit.
   Why hadn't he been believed? What was he supposed to have done when Ambassador Rund chose to remain in the Drow city for years? Leave on his own? Leave without any sort of trade agreement at all, and go where? Back Into the black maze of the Underdark all by himself?  Yi had almost done that, but doing so would have meant death. Did the Empire know of the mind flayers that lived in the depths of the Oerth? Or the wererats? Or the troglodytes? Never mind the drow, who effectively kept him as a prisoner until Rund was released. 
   But he wasn't believed, and Rund was gone, and now he was on a prison ship on the way to Acererak.
   Someone was talking to him. Yi hadn't responded, so the dirty looking Flan was poking his ribs to get his attention. Yi resisted the urge to strike him; the last time he had hit a fellow prisoner hadn't gone down well. He still had an eye that remained half closed. So Yi merely snapped out a curse.
   ""Hey, I'm only trying to help..." retorted the Flan. Yi suddenly became aware that everyone had gone to the other end of the cage, and they were all cowering. The dirty Flan quickly joined them. Yi looked around, puzzled. What had he missed?
   Then he felt a violent shudder. He'd half noticed another one a moment ago, but he had been so lost in misery...
   A loud wrenching crack. It sounded like it was coming from the level directly above him. Yi joined the others.
   Now the entire ship rocked, and crunching noises were everywhere.
   "It's a sea serpent!" cried out a prisoner,, "or a dragon turtle!" cried another. 
   The ship fell sideways, and the prisoners all fell against the bars. A great plank burst and dark water rushed in.
   "Help! We are drowning!"
   Yi was as panicked as the rest. The water was coming into the cage, cold black water from the depths of the Oerth.
   Then he saw an eye. A huge, round unblinking yellow eye. It was looking through the hole. Then the eye disappeared only to be replaced by a long, thick, sinewy black tentacle with vicious hooks upon each sucker.
   Now the prisoners knew what doom awaited them. Not the Isles of Woe. The stomach of a kraken. See less

   The grey Ur Flan sighed. He wasn't sure whether councillor Yi was lying or whether he really didn't know Rund's plan. No matter. It would all sort itself out in the end. Beloved Vecna saw all. Yi would be taken to the Isles of Woe as promised. How long the weedy elfling would last in the pit would be up to lord Acererak.
                                ******
   The ship was bulky, square and barely sea worthy. The sailors hated to crew the cumbersome block of wood, but they held their tongues. The Were Raven was a prison ship, and it was best not to complain lest the sailor ends up in the wrong compartment. The Were Raven bobbed up and down and slightly east atop the Nyr Dyv, the Lake of Unknown Depths. Captain Ink was pleased that the weather held. A few more trips and he hoped to be promoted to a more prestigious ship. The Isles of Woe weren't that bad for him either. He was given a free pass to the arena, and always a good seat above Acererak's pit. The Empire looked after the people it depended on.
   Two days out and the captain was awoken. Fire out to starboard. Ink clambered up to the deck. Out across in the dawn sky, contrasting with the brilliant blue of the deep waters, a ship was aflame. He barked orders and the Were Raven lurched over one way and another until it began to tack in the right direction.
   "We are too late," murmured the captain once they reached the stricken ship, "no survivors."
   But he was wrong. Around midday another crew member spotted a small open boat. Three sailors, wet and disheveled, were taken on board.
   "What happened?" asked Ink.
   "Rebels, " said one survivor sipping their soup, "Their leader was a fierce elfling with long blonde hair. He was looking for someone, a prisoner."
   "That's disturbing news," said Ink, "I don't recall the rebels ever attacking us on the lake before. Who was the prisoner?"
   "Another elfling, I think. Yi was the name."
   "And you weren't carrying him across?"
   "No. Just a shipment of labourers."
   "What happened next?"
   "There was a fight. Our Ur Flan accidentally lit up the ship. Most of the rebels escaped."
   Captain Ink realised that the danger hadn't passed. If the rebels were still seaworthy then they would be looking for another prison ship.
   "First mate, bring me the manifest."
   The manifest was brought forth, then Ink quickly read through the list. One of the slaves was called Yi. Ink ordered a high alert. Before this news the Were Raven could have easily sailed into an ambush. Now they will be ready. 
   Perhaps they would be ready for a rebel ship, but the Nyr Dyv held hidden dangers in her unfathomable depths. The stench of death and blood from the lost sailors had attracted the attention of a black,  tentacled mass of hunger.  An enormous creature of tremendous age and power. A kraken. See less

   Win-Daled was reaching the end of her mortal life.  She had ruled Risewater, home of the Suloise, for many years and the population had  increased,  with further settlements to the North and West.. But the East was off limits, too close to the  Singing Lands.
   Most of her tenure as Suel Chief had been relatively easy. Win-Daled was by far the greatest Arch-mage in the nation, and she had the mighty elven Ye'Cind and the great Flan wunderkind Heward as friends and advisors. 
 The Singing One and the Flan roguish  warrior were fond of wandering though, and lately had been frequenting Risewater less and less. Ye'Cind was still a young elf maiden and Heward seemed to have stopped aging at forty.
    Win-Daled herself felt old, and she was ready to move on to the next stage of existence.She had hoped Heward would take up the job...oh well...his dalliances with the nymphs, dryads and other feminine creatures of Fey was apparently taking up too much of his time for serious work.
    Therefore, Win-Daled chose the son of a gallant former bandit to be her successor. Gryman was intelligent, contemplative and had earned the respect of many of the young Suel in his twenty three years. He was deeply moved by the honour, and promised to serve the Suel faithfully and fairly. Win-Daled assured him that she knew he would.
   At the end of the year, after giving a last speech and wishing everybody well, Win-Daled clutched her heart and fell back on the stage. Her face was serene, and her lips curved with the hint of a smile. She never rose again.
   52 SD, Ye'Cind finally joined up with a small grey elf community that had splintered off from Celene and helped to found a new Elven nation north of the Vast swamp.
   55 SD, Heward, galavanting about Fey, crossed paths with a band of jealous satyrs while in the company of a vivacious nymph. They struck him down and placed him in a  magical prison. There he remained for a long, long time... See less

   Thurnfedge V absently stroked the whip on his lap, the whip taken by Win-Daled from Dweomyne, and the symbol of his legitimate right to rule.
     Norebo looked into the eyes of his king with barely concealed contempt.  Thurnfedge V had watery eyes, devoid of colour. His teeth were clenched and his nose leaked.It was unfortunate that thenoble line had ended up with him. At least he was easily impressed by others, and he fortunately doted upon the sleek Thief Merchant standing before him.
   "Then what is to be done?" asked Thurnfedge helplessly.
   Thurnfedge never knew what was to be done.
    Norebo sighed and pushed a lock of dark hair away from his brow.
   "Leave it with me," he said.  
   In fact, Norebo was not overly concerned with the collapse of the economy in Emeraldrock (which they had been discussing). With Highhold in chaos, and with the Holy Papacy hanging tenuously to its borders, it was going to get pretty rough....
   Norebo knew that his  prosperity was secure, because he was a member of the Oath, a secret society based in the Eastern kingdoms.on the coast of the Solnor sea. The Oath had feelers everywhere. Most of the bandit companies were Oath members, and there were even a handful of Lowly Ones in the Singing Lands who were Brothers.  
   The major Thief Houses were all Oathers, and lucrative trade passed easily between them. The lands around could be poor, but the Oath Society was only increasing its wealth. 
   Norebo knew this, because he was the Merchant Prince overseeing it all.  
   Originally from the east, Norebo had a way of blending in with the Suloise, even with his coppery skin and dark hair. His subtle magic allowed him to be accepted everywhere.. 
   In actuality, Norebo was not concerned about anything much, he found life easy and enjoyable. It was fun to rule behind the scenes watching money flow into Oather coffers. The trick was to stay in the shadows and let the ignorant do the work. See less

   Emeraldrock broke into eight states each ruled by a High Chief and each guarded by a tower and keep. 
   The Holy Papacy of Risewater was as if an island, surrounded by a sea of bandits, humanoids and mercenaries.  
   The elves of the Singing Ones built and prepared for invasion.
   The secret Oath Society was behind it all.
   For the High Chiefs were all Oathers.  Money flowed in from Oathers and out to Oathers. The population hated the bandits, or the Papacy, or the High Chiefs, or the Singing Ones, but it didn't matter, the Oathers were everywhere.
   Mines were reopened, armies were equipped and trained.
   In Risewater the Papacy was firmly under the religion of  the Goddess as interpreted by Pope Syrul, but what she didn't know was that much of the soldiery she employed were secretly Oathers.
In the Singing Lands  key Lowly Ones were Oathers and spied for Thurnfedge V and his adviser Norebo. Bandits counted Oathers amongst their numbers.

   The Svirfneblin were surprised to meet dwarves so deep under the Oerth.  These dwarves were a dour, grey skinned people, who spoke a different dwur language and seemed very defensive and paranoid.
   The duergar didn't know what to make of the gnomes, for the diminutive beings had not yet appeared on Oerth when the duergar last walked under the sun. They took these demi-human buriers to be a potential existential threat, and this meant that the best course of action would be their utter extermination.
   In 459 SD, the duergar began to realise that the Svirfneblin were impossible to eradicate, as they could use magic to disappear into the walls and escape. The Svirfneblin also attempted parleys, for they were not militaristic people.
    Eventually it was decided that a party of duergar would travel to the surface, the Overlight, and learn as much as they could about the new arrivals. What other creatures had followed them to Oerth?
    These duergar were the first of their kind to reach and penetrate the Overlight for thousands of years. They expected a barren, slave world ruled by tall elves with dark magiks.
   Instead of this dystopia, which in fairness, was close to the historical reality when the grey dwur first entered the Underdark, they found a mixture of lands, some elf dominated, but also hills and mountains and plains ruled by dwarves, gnomes, halflings and humans, and life seemed good, prosperous and fair.
   The king of all Dwarves, Moradin Soulforger, did not meet with the duergar, as he surely would have done, because he was currently not on Oerth.
   On another world, far away, a mighty orc had raised a mighty army bent upon total war. Gruumsh was his name, and he was clever, strong, cunning and ambitious. He had somehow gained vast power and had survived blows that would have felled any mortal. Moradin had gone to check the orcish gains.
    Silvervein Moradinson, one of Moradin's mortal descendents, had been appointed Regent for the length of Moradin's absence. Silvervein wielded a stout, magical weapon called the Fierce Axe, or, as it was also known, the Axe of the Dwarven Lords. Silvervein himself had made this great axe alongside Moradin.  The axe conferred authority over all the dwarves of Oerth.  
   So it was Regent Silvervein Moradinson who excitedly met with the duergar delegation from the mysterious Underdark. He hoped to unite with his lost cousins and forge a bright future together. See less

   Oerik was a web, Lolth had said to Elehonna one Spring day, as they walked amongst the ferns and pines of the rainforest surrounding the city.
   Lolth had assumed the guise of a silvery Singing One, as she was more prone to doing these days, instead of her natural, spider-like form. Yet, there was a deeper complexion to her skin, an indigo sheen. And her eyes were deep and violet. Lolth had given herself long hair, but it was of a pale, ghostly hue.
   Elehonna was proud to be Lolth's favourite of all the elves. There was nothing she wouldn't do for her beloved Mistress.
   Oerik was a web, Lolth had said, and the Singing Ones were its spider. They didn't know it, those poor people of the mountains, the valleys, the grasslands, forests and hills. They didn't know it, but they were all insects stuck in the web, and one day... One day Lolth and her Singing One elves would wrap them up tight then suck up their juices.
   Lolth was patient, never in a hurry, and Elehonna believed her to be the wisest being that had ever lived.
 There had been problems controlling the Sheldomar valley, but to the east of the valley were the reforming lands of Celene. Those elves had once been allies of the Singing Lands, but now their sphere of influence had fallen to the Blemu elves further east. 
   Elehonna had been instructed by her Mistress to infiltrate and influence the new Celenian rulers in whatever way she could. A strong Celene, friends of Lolth, would help to crush the Sheldomar rebels.
   Elehonna crossed the Lortmil mountains, then entered into a lightly wooded glade. She had brought with her a troop of the best singers of her land. Before resorting to threats and shows of strength, she hoped to charm the Celenians back into their hedonistic ways.
   The Celenian patrol found the Singing Ones advancing upon the newly repaired road. They hailed them, and the Singing Ones stopped dead, then turned to look at the patrol as one.
   Elehonna and her troop, eyes glazed, tongues lolling, could only utter these words:
   "Hail Tharizdun, our Master."
                ******************
      Pelor led the Company down a sunbeam and into the living heart of Sol.
   The heart was yellow, white and blinding. Small fire elementals sailed to and fro, working great furnaces.
   "This is the Sol Furnace," announced Pelor, "and this is why I wanted you to come to the Sun."
   Yondalla was impressed. It was beautiful. It reminded her of Moradin's Soul Forge in Mount Celestia.
   "I know young Moradin," said Pelor, "his forge is... Adequate. But, this, the Sol Furnace, is greater by far."
   He gestured around animatedly.
   "This place is big, it is vast. In fact, it is much, much larger than the Sun itself."
   Fharlanghn wanted to know what he meant. Celestian looked at his brother and smiled. He thought he knew. He spoke,
   "If I may, great Pelor," he said, "I think I can answer. Most of the stars are suns too, are they not?"
   Pelor nodded.
   "And they are great forces of life and light."
   Pelor nodded again.
   "You are the Sun God, or should I say, Suns God. You are interconnected with all the stars, all the suns."
   "Yes," breathed Pelor.
   "The Sol Furnace is interconnected too. This isn't the heart of the Sun, its the heart of all of the suns."
   "You are right, dear Celestian," said Pelor, "welcome to the heart of every sun in the Universe!" See less

     Corellon Larethian reeled back when the WuzXi elves started screaming. The god had only wanted to communicate with them, but their eyes suddenly glassed over and their mouths opened, high pitched screaming gushing out from their throats. Were they so corrupt that they had forgotten their loving Corellon Larethian?
   Tharizdun sneered when he saw the so-called god Corellon stride up to the group of WuzXi elves  haunting the dead forest and begin asking them questions. Did Corellon not know that the elves were not theirs but his? He lay within their minds, their ultimate master. The WuzXi would say what he wanted them to say, and do what he wanted them to do. 
   The screaming continued without mercy and even Corellon could only take so much. They felt curiously powerless with this strange situation. Mortals were usually reverent, friendly and fearful, not maniacally screaming relentlessly.Then, the god felt a curious touch within his mind, like the tickle of a very soft feather. Something was trying to break in. 
   Tharizdun pulled back an incorporeal tendril and his invisible wispy body billowed out in frustration. This was not the first god he couldn't control. His  power was too limited, it was disappointing.
   The WuzXi stopped screaming but their eyes flashed in anger.
   "Who is there?" Demanded Corellon, "I can see you behind my children's eyes."
   The elves spoke as one, and the cool breeze that drifted amongst the black branches of the petrified trees grew still, as if the air itself was afraid.
   I AM, WE ARE THARIZDUN. THE ELVES ARE MINE."
   Tharizdun, thought Corellon. Bahamut was right. Corellon looked at the fallen elves sternly and raised his hands. A faint golden glow arose from his fingers and drifted out and around the stiff WuzXi.
   The elves laughed, hard, harsh and cold.
   YOU THINK YOU CAN BEST ME, WOOD ELF? YOU HAVE NO PLACE HERE. CRAWL BACK TO YOUR LOG. I DEVOURED THE WUZXI, AND SOON I SHALL DEVOUR ALL OF KARA-TUR. 
   "I can see my magic has no effect upon you," said Corellon Larethian, "but you don't understand the stakes. If I can't make you see reason, you will be stopped, but not by me. The dragons have taken notice."
   The WuzXi smirked with exaggerated grins.
   THE DRAGONS? WHO ARE THESE DRAGONS? THE BROKEN REMNANTS OF A LOST TIME?  LET THEM COME AND TRY TO BEST ME,  FOR IF THEY BE THE DRAGONS' THEN I BE THE DRAGONS' BREATH!
   The WuzXi stepped forward, feet crunching down upon the cracking leaves that carpeted the ground, and as one, drew their swords roughly out of their scabbards .Corellon knew they couldn't be hurt by them, but felt themselves shiver anyway.
   "I fear the dragons will come," said Corellon, "but they bring breath too. And fangs. And claws."
   After uttering these words, Corellon turned away from the WuzXi, sighed, then vanished 
 from the forest. What would be, would be.
   The WuzXi resheathed their swords and looked at each other thoughtfully.
   Tharizdun realised that he had been foolish, because for all his confident bluster, he wasn't really sure what he would or could do if the dragons united against him. Perhaps his pride was still too big for his wisdom. The perils of being young... See less

   Yollanda looked at the shrunken, haggard dwarf within the huge helm of the Dreadnaught and suddenly realised that she recognised him. It was Pious Grimm Quartztusk, the stalwart and stubborn priest of Moradin. What was he doing inside a metal giant? The Dreadnaught jerked closer, gears rattling. Would Pious crush his old friends?
   ""Pious!" She called out, "Pious! What's wrong with you? It's me, Yolanda. I know you can resist this,  for you are a dwur of Moradin!"
   Ulla and Garl, who were desperately thinking of a way to bring the Dreadnaught down, were startled by Yollanda's plea. Yes, it was Pious, their old comrade, but what had happened to him?
   The Mighty Servant lurched itself forward. Pious gritted his teeth and willed the Dreadnaught to stop, but he could not, for he was wholly in the grip of the Dark God Incabulus.
   The crunching feet of the metal monster drew closer to his friends.
   "I must...destroy the tower," murmered Pious, "Step away, I shall not stop."
   Yollanda closed her eyes and mouthed a prayer. A streak of violet light passed out from her hands and burst upon the azure encrusted Dreadnaught. The light fell about Pious's face and he could feel  his mind clearing. He could resist... Yes, he would resist! 
   The Mighty Servant let out a blast of cold air - a metallic sigh. It clanked, then stopped dead.
   Ye'Cind was confused, as was Heward, who had become invisible once more and was cautiously peering around the tower. The elf wizard and the human rogue didn't know Pious because they had not fought with him on Toril.
   Pious Grimm let out a gasp of fear. His brain felt like it was being squeezed inside his skull. It seemed Incabulus would not let him go so easily. Pious whimpered with the pain, could he overthrow the will of his new master?
   (Incabulus, far away within the Cain Hills,  shrieked in rage. He would not be thwarted.)
   The Dreadnaught rattled, a deep, dark, diabolical rattle that passed along the great Agrar hill and struck the side of the tower with a mighty slap. Yolanda, Ye'Cind, Garl Glittergold, Ulla and Heward felt their bones literally shake. The shaking increased, intensifying rapidly. The tower seemed to vibrate, then Yolanda shrieked and she clutched her ribs, they were splitting and cracking apart!
   Ye'Cind and Garl were flung to the ground. Ulla resisted the shockwave for a little longer, bracing herself with her strong dwarvish body, used to hard work within the mountains, but the vibrations were rattling her teeth loose. Heward simply disappeared.
   Inside the Servant,  Pious, sweat beading his brow, tried to cease the  unholy rattling that was destroying his friends. He still felt the quiet, clear light that shone warmly about him, and was slowly overcoming his pain. He would regain control. He would stop the Dreadnaught.
   And the shaking and the rattling stopped. Yollanda, Garl, Ye'Cind were lying motionless, dead or alive, no one knew. Ulla was clutching her throbbing jaw. 
   (Incabulus seethed, but Pious was strongly resisting. Would he escape his control?)
   Pious felt his heart pumping, almost like his old self.  He had overcome the evil god that was clutching him against its black heart.
   Then, a loud explosion shook the Mighty Servant and Pious had to pull levers quickly to keep himself upright. The tower had lifted itself off the ground and was streaking up into the sky.
   In  the tower control room, grim faced, Maglubiyet, hovering over his Machine, bruised and battered from the Servant's attack on the tower, smiled despite the pain, because he knew what he would do to those that came against him in his own realm. He flicked three switches and turned two dials on the panel before him. His Machine had magic never rseen before on Oerth.Now, all Hell would break loose. See less

   Several more days went past. Eventually Rund managed to garner a couple of spies who worked in Vecna's tower. Rund's pockets were deep, and his sword very sharp, as the would-be pickpockets and thieves soon discovered. The news came back. Councillor Yi was locked in a guest room, definitely very much alive, but the major news was about Vecna himself. No one wanted to be near him, for he was roused in a great temper. As to why? Nobody knew.
                               ******
   "Get dressed in your finest clothes," said the slave, coming into the room, because you are about to have a most important visitor."
   Yi didn't have much to choose from, but he did his best. It sounded like the Emperor was on his way to see him, and that was good news. If Vecna was coming to him and not the other way around then Ambassador Rund might well have been telling him the truth. Vecna had realised that the real Book of Vile Darkness had been recovered, and Yi was about to be rewarded.
   But it wasn't Vecna who lumbered into the room, but the monstrous Secretary Spindle. Spindle's skin was as thick as boot leather, and his face was distinctly goblinoid. He had one long and thin arm that resembled a half-dead tree branch, and his legs were like those of a rhinoceros.
   The rumours said that Spindle had died a hundred years ago but no one had informed his body.
   "Councillor Yi," said the Secretary, "the hospitality is over."
   "What's happening?" asked Yi.
   "You are being evicted, that's what."
   "What about the book...?"
   Spindle loomed over the elfling, "you dare to ask about that damned book?"
   Yi held firm, "I brought our beloved Vecna the book, and he asked me to wait here until he reached a decision."
   Spindle smiled savagely, "Exactly, Councillor, Vecna has reached a decision. He has chosen the true Book, and he has utterly rejected the forgery."
   "Well, that's good for me, unless the book I brought him was the wrong one...?"
   "Oh ho! Aren't you sure? Were you lying all this time?"
   "I told Vecna the truth. I believe that I recovered a stolen book. I believe that it's the true book, but..."
   "You brought him the right Book alright. He is keeping the one that you gave him."
   Yi's face brightened, "that's good. But why then am I to be evicted?"
   "Evicted and exiled. Once you leave the tower you must also leave Spar and the Flanaess entire."
   "Exiled? I don't understand...?"
   The Secretary hissed through his tusk-like teeth, "Vecna might have the right book, but choosing it has driven him into a tremendous rage. He curses you, though you were true, for you have proven to the Emperor that he was deceived. No one else but us can know, and his gratitude alone spares you, for otherwise you would already be dead."
   Yi became forlorn, "I love the Empire. I love my Emperor."
   "And that is why you will say nothing, and you will leave now. Naturally, if I hear even one word... And remember, Vecna sees everything."
                              ******
   Yi reached the bottom landing of the tower when he was greeted by an Ur Flan in dark grey ring mail with a black cloak. 
   "Yi," he said, "you must come with me before you leave." He led Yi out of the tower and into a cobbled lane.
   "Where are we going?" asked Yi nervously, for he had no plans to tally and risk the Secretary's wrath. 
   "Vecna has ordered me to take you to the refuse pile. He has a parting gift put aside for you."
   The lane was narrow and dirty and led to a couple of huts and a few mounds of waste from the city. Behind one of the piles, Yi heard a growl. Emerging into sight was a large grey dog with two heads.
   One of Secretary Spindle's death dogs!
   Four bloodshot eyes glared at him, but the death dog did no more than growl.
   "Pay the dog no heed," said the Ur Flan, "he is just here to make sure that you accept your gift."
